title: Isomorphisms descend along etale surjections
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of bounded
constructible complexes on $X$. If $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism,
then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Apply [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover] to the singleton family $\{u\}$. It is a pro-etale cover of $X$; in particular $u$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

source.place: Tag 098B, label lemma-etale-proetale (the finite-affine-refinement covering argument is delegated to the existing covering node).

proof.text: Since $\ell\neq p=\operatorname{char}k$ by [def-pur-conventions], $\ell$ is invertible on the $k$-schemes $X$ and $U$, and $u$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by step 1. The objects $M,N$ of the full subcategory $D^b_c(X,A)$ are objects of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Apply [lem-pur-finite-pullback-localization-cohomology] to $u$, $K=M$, $L=N$ and $\psi=\varphi$. Its naturality equation $c^r_N\circ\mathcal H^r(Lu^*\varphi)=R_U(h_r)\circ c^r_M$, with $c^r_M,c^r_N$ isomorphisms, identifies $\mathcal H^r(Lu^*\varphi)$ with $R_U(h_r)$, where $h_r=\mathcal H^r(\varphi)$. Since $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism, so is its image under every cohomology functor, and hence every $R_U(h_r)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CE, label lemma-localize-given-products, in the normalized derived module form stated in lem-pur-finite-pullback-localization-cohomology.

proof.text: Fix $r$. By the formula $(R_UF)(W\to U)=F(W\to X)$ of [lem-pur-finite-pullback-localization-cohomology], the underlying morphism of set-valued sheaves of $R_U(h_r)$, read on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ through the site identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], is the restriction $h_r|_U$ of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; it is an isomorphism by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with its covering topology, the category of sets, the single object $C=(U\xrightarrow{u}X)$ and the underlying set-sheaf morphism of $h_r$. Its covering hypothesis holds: for an object $V$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the base-change axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] applied to the covering $\{u\}$ of the final object $X$ of step 1 makes $\{V\times_XU\to V\}$ a covering, and its arrow factors through the projection $V\times_XU\to U$; this also covers $X=\emptyset$ and $V=\emptyset$. Hence $(h_r)_T$ is bijective for every object $T$. Its inverse is additive, $A_X(T)$-linear and compatible with restrictions, since each of these equations follows after applying the injective map $(h_r)_T$. Consequently $h_r$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, label lemma-glue-maps (maps of sheaves glue on a covering); cover-local isomorphism criterion as stated in lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism (Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop).

proof.text: All the cohomology maps $\mathcal H^r(\varphi)$ are now isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] to the abelian category of $A_X$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. It follows that $\varphi$ is invertible in the ambient derived category. The bounded constructible category is full, so this inverse is also an inverse in the category of the statement. This proves the required implication without any extra Tor-amplitude or etale-origin hypothesis.
